NIT Rourkela Researchers Develop Innovative Fractal Antenna for Advanced Wireless Communication

Researchers from the Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering at the National Institute of Technology (NIT) Rourkela have developed an innovative wideband circularly polarized hybrid fractal antenna designed to improve the reliability and performance of wireless communication systems. The technology holds potential for point-to-point wireless communication, particularly in applications where signal interference and multipath fading pose significant challenges.

The research, conducted by Mr. Prasannajeet Mohanty and Prof. Santanu Kumar Behera of the RF & Microwave Systems Group, combines two advanced geometric designs, known as Hexaflake and Modified Tree fractal structures, to achieve wide bandwidth, high radiation efficiency and stable signal transmission.

Unlike conventional antennas, the proposed design uses circular polarization, which helps reduce signal degradation caused by reflections, interference and changes in antenna orientation. This makes the antenna particularly promising for wireless communication systems operating in complex environments.

The antenna operates across a wide frequency range of 1.75 to 3.55 GHz, achieving an impedance bandwidth of 68%. It demonstrates a peak realized gain of 3.17 dBic and radiation efficiency exceeding 89% within its operational band. The researchers also achieved right-hand circular polarization (RHCP) through a specially designed fractal structure, with a measured axial-ratio bandwidth of 2.35–2.42 GHz.

Fabricated using a commonly available FR4 substrate, the antenna offers a compact design with promising performance characteristics. Experimental measurements closely matched the simulated results, validating the effectiveness of the proposed technology.

The development has potential applications in L-band, S-band and Industrial, Scientific and Medical (ISM) frequency-band wireless systems. Its ability to mitigate multipath fading and interference could contribute to more reliable wireless connectivity. The researchers aim to further enhance the antenna's gain to explore its suitability for longer-distance point-to-point communication links.

The research findings have been published in the peer-reviewed international Journal of Electromagnetic Waves and Applications, highlighting NIT Rourkela's continued contributions to research and innovation in wireless communication and antenna engineering.
